examples.japanese: {白玉粉|しらたまこ}で{団子|だんご}を{作|つく}る。
examples.english: To make dumplings with glutinous rice flour.

examples.japanese: {白玉粉|しらたまこ}に{水|みず}を{少|すこ}しずつ{加|くわ}えて{練|ね}る。
examples.english: Add water little by little to the glutinous rice flour and knead.

examples.japanese: {白玉粉|しらたまこ}で{作|つく}った{白玉|しらたま}を{冷|つめ}たい{あんみつ|あんみつ}に{入|い}れると{夏|なつ}にぴったりのデザートになる。
examples.english: Adding shiratama dumplings made from glutinous rice flour to chilled anmitsu makes a perfect summer dessert.

notes:
A fine flour made from glutinous rice ({もち米|もちごめ}), used primarily to make {白玉|しらたま} (small, chewy rice dumplings). The dumplings are served in traditional Japanese desserts like {ぜんざい|ぜんざい}, {あんみつ|あんみつ}, and {みつまめ|みつまめ}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {白玉粉|しらたまこ}を{練|ね}る: to knead glutinous rice flour
- {白玉粉|しらたまこ}で{団子|だんご}を{作|つく}る: to make dumplings with rice flour

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {上新粉|じょうしんこ}: non-glutinous rice flour — made from regular rice, producing a firmer texture
- {もち粉|もちこ}: mochi flour — similar to {白玉粉|しらたまこ} but ground differently; more common in Western markets
- {片栗粉|かたくりこ}: potato starch — used as a thickener; not a rice flour
